brief:
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell as investors digested the impact of higher oil prices and inflation concerns, with the 10-year yield rising amid anticipation of a hotter-than-expected September core inflation rate.

S&P 500 (-0.78% to 7744.72): Earnings Season and Inflation Concerns. The S&P 500 fell 0.78% to 7744.72 as investors digested the impact of higher oil prices and memory chip stock losses, which pressured the market. [1] [2] [4] The market's decline was also influenced by concerns about inflation, which led to a rise in yields and a subsequent sell-off. [3]
Nasdaq (-1.09% to 26907.76): Nasdaq Falls Amid Tech Weakness. The Nasdaq fell 1.09% to 26907.76, with most high-profile tech stocks weakening, as investors bet on a rate hike due to higher-than-expected CPI [5]. The global AI selloff also intensified, contributing to the Nasdaq's decline [6]. The decline was part of a broader market downturn, with the S&P 500 and Dow also falling, as investors reacted to earnings season and higher oil prices [1, 2, 4].
10-Year Yield (+1.05% to 5.27): Yields Rise Amid Inflation Concerns. The 10-year yield rose as investors anticipated a hotter-than-expected September core inflation rate, which could prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy further. [9] This move was also driven by investors seeking higher yields in a US Treasury rout, as seen in [10]. [8] suggests that the Fed may still tighten further, contributing to the yield rise. [7]
USD/JPY (+0.21% to 158.86): USD/JPY Surges on Inflation Concerns. The USD/JPY pair rose 0.21% to 158.86 as traders reacted to inflation shock in the US, prompting a surge in the US dollar. This move may be attributed to traders watching crude oil and US yields, as mentioned by BigGo Finance. The Japanese yen is approaching September lows, according to FXStreet, and may continue to weaken against the US dollar.
Crude Oil (+0.98% to 95.06): Oil Prices Rise Amid Tensions. Traders are watching the escalating tensions in the Middle East, particularly the reported attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, which has raised concerns about the stability of global oil supplies. [17] [15] [18] The news has led to a rise in oil prices, with crude oil rising 0.98% to 95.06. [1]
Gold (-1.58% to 4111.3): Gold Falls on Inflation Concerns. Gold prices fell overnight as traders anticipated a potential interest rate hike to combat rising inflation. The expectation of higher interest rates led to a decrease in gold prices, as investors shifted their focus to safer assets. This move is also driven by the recent data on US CPI, which showed a rise in inflation, further fueling the interest rate hike bets.

Also worth knowing:
- The Dow rose ahead of CPI inflation data, but Bank of America's results led to a decline.
- Stocks dropped and Treasury yields surged after a hot inflation reading, with memory stocks extending declines.
- A Fed rate hike call is seen tight as inflation heats up, with Bullard predicting two hikes and hope from the Federal Reserve.

This is a concern for uranium companies [37, 38].
